title: Bloody Sunset
subtitle: Practice the art of listening by allowing others to express their opinions before you make yours known.

items.text: Bloody Sunset
Midnight Club

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: ... You can only taste this in Paris. Its name will never appear on any menu.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Dark red, like the blood of a sinner.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: From the first taste, you'd never imagine it's made from grapes alone.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: It has a dryness that parches the throat until you start to crave its warmth again. Like a hungry vampire, you'll never be sated, always seeking another sip.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Then you're hooked, my dear. Each day onwards is spent waiting in anticipation for the next "Bloody Sunset."
Adelita takes a sip and lets slip a rare smile.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: My, my. This truly is an extraordinary vintage. You may just be sincere after all, Brette.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Words like that are sweet pleasure to my ears.
Adelita and "Brette" share the rare "Bloody Sunset" as time slips away with the faint ticking of the corner clock.
At nine forty-two, Adelita has only a single swallow left.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: As a matter of pride, I always reward a good turn.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Hearing that, I can't help but look forward to a gift from you.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: What I'll give you is a possibility, just as you gave me the "Bloody Sunset."
Adelita reaches into her jellyfish-shaped handbag and produces a small box bedazzled with jewels, its delicate silver inlay hinting at great value.
Meanwhile, the arms dealer, looking worn, arrives back at the bar.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: As you can see, I've returned with time to spare.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What's that you're drinking?

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: "Bloody Sunset." Brette recommended it to me. I promise, once you taste it, you'll never forget it.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: If you say so, I'll give it a try.
Adelita drains the last drop from her glass.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: A pity, Mr. Longen. Adelita just had the final one.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: That's right. The last "Bloody Sunset" in this establishment, this city, maybe the country.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I don't appreciate being toyed with, Adelita.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Fleming waves the subject aside, annoyed.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Drelome was drunk out of his mind. I couldn't get a word in edgewise.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I hope at least you kept my guest entertained, Madame Cosette.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Naturally, and I must say your timing is impeccable. Adelita was just about to show me a little surprise.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: A surprise? Well, go on; I could use something to pick me up.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Of course. Come closer.
The two lean in as Adelita flicks open the tiny bronze latch.
With a crisp click, the box reveals a velvet cushion—empty where a jewel should rest.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: There's nothing inside.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: To gain anything, one must first pay a price. The first and unchanging rule of commerce.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Price?

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: This box is the life's work of a South African pure-blooded arcanist. I call it the "Box from the South."

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: All you have to do is put a diamond on the velvet cushion, then turn the hidden mechanism inside the lid, following the instructions—

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Eight hours later, when you reopen it, you'll find another identical diamond beside it.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Whatever do you make of that, Mr. Longen?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Hah.
A wry laugh escapes him.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: It's quite the story, I'll say that for sure.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: But I've got to figure that if this thing were really spitting out diamonds, then every crook from L.A. to Sicily would be after you.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: The kind of thing you don't carry around if you know what's good for you.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Every treasure has its first discoverer, Mr. Longen.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: When Marshall found gold at Sutter's Mill, only a handful of locals knew of his find—at first.
The minute hand passes forty-five, but none of them mention the time.
The "Box from the South" lies open in Adelita's palm, awaiting the presence of a diamond.
The arms dealer studies it, caught between doubt and desire.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... In my experience, anything tied to arcanum is the furthest thing from trustworthy.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: The way I see it, there's a simple way to test our charming lady's claim.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What? You want to put a diamond inside and then lock it away for eight hours?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I can't see a reason why not. Though, perhaps a stipulation is due.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: If the box does not yield another diamond. Then, Ms. Adelita will pay us its value in compensation.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: That's still a big risk. Who's going to look after it? I'm not really keen on watching a box all night.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I'm certain we can find a safe somewhere here. So, why don't we lock it inside there?

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Allow me to set the combination, and you may hold the key. That way neither of us can touch it until our next meeting.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: That works. I can vouch for the owner.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I'm game, but ...
He feels as though he's about to make a serious gamble, but then again ... what if this is another "Sutter's Mill"?

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: It's a game in your favor, Fleming. One way or another, you gain.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I'll even arrange the collateral—money equal to the value of two diamonds.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: If the box works, you keep the diamond and return my money.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: And even if Adelita disappears, you still have the collateral.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Seems like a game worth playing to me.
Tennant stands between them, playing the part of a less than impartial judge.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Even if I wanted to play, where would I get a diamond at this hour?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: My dear Fleming, you seem to have forgotten our conversation; allow me—
A pea-sized crystal glimmers in Tennant's hand, as if conjured from thin air.
A round-cut diamond, brilliant and flawless, flashing dazzling light across its 58 facets.
After letting it shine, Tennant closes it back into her hand.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Mined from Panna, India. One and a half carats. Near-colorless. Internally flawless. Excellent cut.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What are the odds of that?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: The odds of a jewel dealer having a jewel on her person? My dear Mr. Longen, I shouldn't imagine it would surprise you.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I just so happen to always have a few samples on hand for clients.
The logic of the statement puts Fleming at ease.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Okay. I'm in. But what's this thing worth?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: At market price, I would suggest twenty thousand francs. So, two would make forty thousand.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Would that be agreeable to both of you?
The arms dealer lowers his head, mind racing.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: So, if I've got this right. Out of the gate, I'm up twenty thousand. Enough to cover my expenses.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: And if this thing's a phony, I walk away with forty thousand?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... For that matter, if this diamond of yours disappears, that's your problem as far as I can see.
The sharp-nosed merchant smells opportunity. His eyes gleam.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Sounds like a deal.
Tennant sets the diamond on the velvet, and Adelita snaps the lid shut.
The clock strikes ten.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Come, Mr. Longen. Let's ask the manager for a safe.
